title: He Built a $40k/Month Side Hustle Before Quitting His Job (Here's How)
promo_conflict: The host directs viewers to Campour Nation and related episodes; no paid promotion is disclosed in the transcript.

stated_problem.quote: Is this really what the next 30 years is going to look like, staring at the same cubicle walls
stated_problem.speaker: Phil

idea.name: Campour Nation high-ticket e-commerce store
idea.one_liner: An online store reselling established camper van, RV, caravan and motor-home brands, initially through dropshipping; it later added inventory and is considering its own products.
idea.customer: Camper van, RV, caravan and motor-home owners
idea.offer: High-ticket accessories from established suppliers, with product guidance and phone support before purchase.
idea.revenue_model: Retail margin on supplier products; supplier ships orders initially, with some inventory held later. The business is considering manufacturing branded products.

key_quotes.quote: Phil took his side hustle, an e-commerce store selling a camper van, accessories to 40 grand a month, while still working his day job.
I went very much after products that are retailing for $1,000 plus, and so you could be making, you know, anything from $150 up to a few thousand dollars of profit in every sale on one of those.
The big thing we're trying to do at the start really is we're going after the traffic that's going to come from the absolute bottom funnel searches on Google.
We've done, um, you know, 1200, 1500 orders over the last 18 months and I think we've had 10 12 returns maybe in that time.
I pay a few dollars per per article to follow along a very specific SOP that we've built
For me, that was hitting 40,000 in revenue a month for six months in a row.

claims.claim: The host says the store reached $40,000 in monthly sales while Phil still had his job.
claims.quote: Phil took his side hustle, an e-commerce store selling a camper van, accessories to 40 grand a month, while still working his day job.

claims.claim: The host says a sale could yield between $150 and $50,000 profit.
claims.quote: He could be making, you know, anything from $150 up to $50,000 of profit in every sale on one of those.

claims.claim: The host says the business later reached $120,000 in monthly sales.
claims.quote: Since then, he's grown to $120,000 a month in sales, and he did it not by inventing his own products, but by partnering with brands that already had demand.

claims.claim: The guest says he launched with products from four brands.
claims.quote: I got four brands for my site when I started.

claims.claim: The guest chose products retailing above $1,000 and says a sale could make $150 to a few thousand dollars profit.
claims.quote: I went very much after products that are retailing for $1,000 plus, and so you could be making, you know, anything from $150 up to a few thousand dollars of profit in every sale on one of those.

claims.claim: The guest uses $10 and $15 items as examples of low-ticket products that require many sales to replace income.
claims.quote: You've got to sell a lot of $10, $15 products to make the sort of money that's going to ultimately replace your income

claims.claim: The guest's niche research looked for a combined 20 million or more monthly searches.
claims.quote: I was looking for something in the region of a total collection of those of 20,000,000 plus monthly searches from them

claims.claim: The guest considers 20 or more direct online competitors too competitive in the US.
claims.quote: I think in the US 20 plus direct competitors, and I don't mean Amazon or big boss stores, I mean someone else who's basically doing a similar or the same business model as me

claims.claim: The guest estimates he contacted around 20 suppliers before launching.
claims.quote: I think I'd maybe reached out to 20 or something

claims.claim: The guest says one supplier approval is enough to start making sales.
claims.quote: all you need is one yes to get a start and you can make sales with that.

claims.claim: The guest considered 10 or more potential suppliers a good number for a niche.
claims.quote: We were kind of looking at sort of 10 plus was a good number to be able to get

claims.claim: The guest says upper-funnel clicks cost two to five pence in his campaigns.
claims.quote: that upper funnel traffic, that generic sauna type traffic, I'm bidding anywhere between two pence and five pence on that.

claims.claim: The guest says lower-funnel clicks can cost about £1 to £5.
claims.quote: Quite often it's somewhere in between pound to five pounds, but yeah, that's the type of CPCs that you'd be sort of expecting to see in that.

claims.claim: The guest reports seeing gross margins of 15% to 40% across products.
claims.quote: I've seen anywhere between, um, 15 to 40 percent, um, gross margins on stuff.

claims.claim: The guest says products above $10,000 may have 15% to 20% margins.
claims.quote: I think if you've got really high ticket stuff, you 10, 20,000 dollars plus, you might see more like the 15 to 20 percent range in some cases

claims.claim: The guest says products closer to $1,000 typically have 25% to 30% margins.
claims.quote: but I think on stuff that's getting a bit closer to that 1,000 mark, something typical around 25, 30 percent is, um, is pretty standard.

claims.claim: The guest discusses offering 100-day returns against competitors offering 30 days.
claims.quote: if everyone else is advertising 30 day returns and I'm doing a hundred and someone buys from me, maybe my supplier only has a 30 day returns window.

claims.claim: The guest says the business processed 1,200 to 1,500 orders over 18 months and had about 10 to 12 returns.
claims.quote: We've done, um, you know, 1200, 1500 orders over the last 18 months and I think we've had 10 12 returns maybe in that time.

claims.claim: The guest describes SEO tiers of 0–10, 10–20 and 20–50 daily visitors.
claims.quote: So for example, if you're getting between 0 and 10 daily visitors from Google, you're in level zero. If you're getting 10 to 20, you're in level one, 20 to 50 level two.

claims.claim: The guest uses a site with five daily organic visitors as an example of a site unlikely to rank for a broad keyword.
claims.quote: So my site with its five daily organic visitors is never going to never going to be able to rank for that word

claims.claim: The guest suggests articles might each bring 10, 20 or 50 visitors.
claims.quote: You build lots of those articles that are maybe all going to bring in 10, 20, 50 visitors to them

claims.claim: The guest describes building 100 articles to create an organic traffic base.
claims.quote: build a hundred of those and all of a sudden you've got a base of organic traffic

claims.claim: The guest pays a freelancer a few dollars per article.
claims.quote: I pay a few dollars per per article to follow along a very specific SOP that we've built

claims.claim: The guest waited until monthly revenue reached $40,000 for six consecutive months before leaving his job.
claims.quote: For me, that was hitting 40,000 in revenue a month for six months in a row.

claims.claim: The guest says bulk orders might improve margins by 10% to 15% or more.
claims.quote: If you can place a bulk order supply, you might get 10%, 15% better margin on those products, maybe more.

claims.claim: The guest refers to products retailing for a couple of thousand pounds when describing the benefit of bulk-order margins.
claims.quote: And when you're talking about maybe a product that retails for a couple of thousand pounds, that's meaningful additional money.

acquisition_channels.details: Calls supplier sales managers and applies through authorized-retailer pages to secure supplier relationships.
Google Shopping Ads, initially targeting bottom-funnel product searches.
Organic search content, including product comparisons, guides and informational articles.

ideas.delivery: Campour lists supplier products on its e-commerce site. Suppliers initially dropship orders to customers; the business handles pre-sale questions by phone and coordinates returns. It later began holding best-selling stock and using a 3PL, while outsourcing much post-sale support. It is considering its own manufactured products.

prices: $150 to a few thousand dollars potential profit per sale
a couple of thousand pounds retail

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to customer and order data; online consumer sales bring distance-selling cancellation and consumer-rights obligations. Screen cold business calls against TPS/CTPS. No subscription model is described.
